task.title: Working from home
task.scenario: Many companies now let employees work from home for some days each week.
task.prompt: Write about the advantages and disadvantages of working from home. Which do you think is stronger?
instructions: Make sure you cover all of the points below.
You are writing for: readers of a general-interest website. Style: neutral.

expected_response.discourse_complexity: One to three paragraphs or a connected multi-sentence turn.
expected_response.linguistic_demand: Connected paragraphs on familiar and some abstract topics; narration, opinion with reasons; range of linkers; basic complex sentences.
expected_response.cognitive_demand: Weigh advantages and disadvantages; Compare and contrast two options

examples.label: Illustrative outline only - not an answer key; many other responses are equally valid

learning_objectives.text: Write a balanced text that presents advantages and disadvantages and gives a view

difficulty.language_demand: Connected paragraphs on familiar and some abstract topics; narration, opinion with reasons; range of linkers; basic complex sentences.
difficulty.cognitive_demand: Weigh advantages and disadvantages; Compare and contrast two options
expected_performance: Covers all required points with some detail; purpose and audience are clear; opinions or events are supported at a basic level.
Ideas connected into paragraphs or a clear sequence; a range of basic linkers and some reference words used.
Adequate range for familiar topics; some less common words attempted; mostly correct word choice and spelling.
difficulty.rationale: Heuristic components (0=A1 .. 5=C2): {'grammar': 1.5, 'cognition': 2.5, 'length': 2.21, 'abstractness': 2.0, 'prompt_language': 1.51}; composite 1.94 -> B1. Original target B1. Computed from invited grammar, cognitive operations, expected length, abstractness and prompt language only.

criteria.name: Task fulfilment
criteria.description: How fully and appropriately the response does what the task asks: required points, purpose, audience and, where relevant, position.
criteria.successful_performance: Covers all required points with some detail; purpose and audience are clear; opinions or events are supported at a basic level. Required points: two advantages; two disadvantages; your overall view
criteria.weak_performance: Some points missing or only listed; opinion stated without reasons; partly off topic.
criteria.expected_evidence: Which required points are present; how each is supported; whether purpose, audience and position are clear. Check each required point: two advantages; two disadvantages; your overall view.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Content knowledge is not assessed; do not penalise factual inaccuracy unless the task asks for accuracy to a supplied source.

criteria.name: Coherence and cohesion
criteria.description: How logically the ideas connect and how clearly linking devices and reference express those connections.
criteria.successful_performance: Ideas connected into paragraphs or a clear sequence; a range of basic linkers and some reference words used.
criteria.weak_performance: Linkers are repeated or misused; paragraphing unclear.
criteria.expected_evidence: Order of ideas; variety and accuracy of linkers; clarity of pronoun reference; paragraph logic.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: A text can be cohesive and still weak on content; keep this criterion separate from task fulfilment.

criteria.name: Lexical resource
criteria.description: Range, precision and appropriateness of vocabulary, including collocation and word formation.
criteria.successful_performance: Adequate range for familiar topics; some less common words attempted; mostly correct word choice and spelling.
criteria.weak_performance: Repetitive vocabulary; word-choice errors sometimes obscure meaning.
criteria.expected_evidence: Range of topic words; repetition; collocation; word formation; spelling. Expected vocabulary demands: work and office life; advantage / disadvantage language; time and money.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Do not reward unusual words that are used incorrectly; do not penalise a plain word that is correct and appropriate.

l1_transfer_hypotheses.caution: These are hypotheses about common patterns; they are NOT to be reported as a learner weakness from a single instance.

criteria.name: Grammatical range and accuracy
criteria.description: Range of structures used and the accuracy with which they are controlled, including punctuation that affects clarity.
criteria.successful_performance: Mix of simple and complex sentences; tenses mostly controlled; errors do not impede communication.
criteria.weak_performance: Frequent errors in complex sentences; limited range; errors sometimes obscure meaning.
criteria.expected_evidence: Types of structures; proportion of error-free sentences; kinds of errors; whether errors are systematic. Structures invited by the task: comparatives_superlatives, linking_words, conditionals_real.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Judge by the structures the learner chooses and controls; do not penalise absence of structures the task does not invite.

l1_transfer_hypotheses.caution: These are hypotheses about common patterns; they are NOT to be reported as a learner weakness from a single instance.

criteria.name: Organisation and development of ideas
criteria.description: Overall structure of the text and how far main ideas are developed, supported and linked to a position or purpose.
criteria.successful_performance: Clear opening and ending; main points are given with a reason or example.
criteria.weak_performance: Points stated without development; no clear opening or ending.
criteria.expected_evidence: Presence of position/thesis; paragraph topics; reasons and examples per point; conclusion.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Do not apply to very short A1/A2 texts; the task does not require essay structure there.

not_assessed_by_design.name: Register and appropriateness
not_assessed_by_design.reason: Not required by this task type at this level, so it must not be used to reduce the score.

required_demonstrations: Address every required point: two advantages; two disadvantages; your overall view
Use language appropriate to: readers of a general-interest website
not_penalised: absence of advanced structures (inversion, mixed conditionals)

target_level_attainment.1: partial: some target-level features, frequent breakdowns
target_level_attainment.2: mostly secure: target-level features present with some lapses

evaluation_blueprint.notes: The illustrative outline in expected_response.examples is NOT an answer key. Accept any response that fulfils the task.

policy.observed_error_vs_weakness: A diagnostic category is an OBSERVED error pattern when at least one instance is found in a response. It may be reported as an INFERRED learning weakness only after >= 3 instances in one response set of >= 100 words (or >= 2 responses) and when the error is not explained by task demands (for example a tense the task did not invite).

diagnostics.observed_vs_inferred: An error is OBSERVED when an instance appears in the response. It may be recorded as an INFERRED weakness only under the policy in diagnostics.policy (repeated instances, enough text, and not explained by task demands).
